newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on hedges, CBOT soycomplex.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on hedges, CBOT soycomplex.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended down on hedge selling and lower CBOT soycomplex values, traders said.

"There were good hedges into the close," a trader said. Jan-Mar spread at $3.20, Jan-May $4.30. January futures crush profit margin fell to -35.29 from -34.76 on Friday. Volume was 2,860 lots, or 57,200 tonnes, with 310 hedge lots.
January canola fell $2.30 to $396.80, March lost $2.80 to $399.70. January flax was unchanged at $345 on crusher demand and short-covering, March fell $2 to $349. Jan-Mar at $3.70.
Barley set contract lows across the board as the February lost $1.60 to $134.50, March fell $1.60 to $132.40.
About 500 Feb-May barley spread at even money then $0.50, Feb-July even money, May-July $0.10. Volume was 1,650 lots.
March feed wheat lost $3 to $166, May fell $3.40 to $163.10 under pressure from U.S. feed grain markets.
"That lower USDA hog number (Friday) is negative for us in the long term," a feed wheat trader said.

October oats were sold down US$1.50 to US$111 by Royal Bank of Canada-Dominion Securities to LFG, traders said. RBCDS sold July down US$2 to US$111 and May down US$2 to US$110 to UGG and another commercial, they said. Volume was 45. Peas did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
